hintProposals.reason: The source states only 秦時, not a regnal year or Western year. The asserted BC 239 requires an independently pinned chronology of Cheng Jiao’s rebellion; the source alone cannot establish the point conversion.

見於始皇本紀 is a bibliographic citation, not a dated event of the First Emperor. It cannot support an AD/BC activity interval; the asserted BC 221–210 is an imported reign span rather than chronology expressed by this unit.
The source credits Han Gao-hou with abolishing the three-clans order but supplies no reign year. BC 187 is not source-established and needs an independent legal-history witness before retention.

The source names Emperor Wen’s legal actions and later quotes him, but gives no regnal years. The point dates BC 179 and BC 167 require independently pinned evidence for each event and cannot be approved from these undated passages.

北魏 identifies Cui Ting’s political setting but supplies neither a date nor a personal activity interval. AD 480–520 is a dynasty-wide span, not evidence that Cui Ting was active throughout it; research must establish the cited saying and chronology or remove the range.
The phrase is an undated historical allusion within Cui Ting’s quotation. BC 500 is not stated and requires a source-specific chronology of the Sima Niu–Huan Tui episode.
